They may also experience vision problems such as nystagmus (rapid involuntary eye movements), photophobia (sensitivity to bright lights), and reduced visual acuity. Treatment options for oculocutaneous albinism focus on managing symptoms and improving quality of life through measures such as sunglasses, hats, and sunscreen protection. Genetic counseling and testing may help families understand their risk of passing on the disorder to future generations. Overall, while there is no cure for oculocutaneous albinism, early diagnosis and appropriate management can significantly improve outcomes for affected individuals.
